fact_checks: The verified facts confirm api.operation.realizes.application.applicationfunction exists, and realizes is the only predicate from api.operation to application.applicationfunction.
The facts list no relationship in the reverse direction, so the alternative 'function realizes operation' is not currently modelled.

The function's definition says it is 'invoked from inside the system rather than offered as a contract to external consumers' and that it realizes the ApplicationService. That fits poorly with an externally exposed API operation realizing it.
The facts do not show whether api.operation has any relationship to application.applicationservice, so the claim's suggested replacement cannot be confirmed or refuted as already present.

arguments_for: The function definition calls it internal and non-contractual, yet an API operation, which is an external contract, is the only cross-layer realizer shown. This contradicts the layer's own distinctions.
The ApplicationService distinction names 'endpoint-backed capability' as service territory. An operation should therefore attach to services, not functions.
Modellers mapping endpoints will read this edge as license to link operations to internal functions, which blurs the service/function boundary the spec draws.
arguments_against: Cross-layer realizes edges in this spec typically run from more concrete layers to more abstract ones. An API operation concretely implementing a function is a coherent reading.
The facts don't show a missing operation-to-service link, so the edge may be supplementary rather than mistaken.
Removing the only realizer may orphan functions from API traceability in CLI validation.

arguments_for: The predicate 'realizes' is defined as 'implements or makes concrete'. An operation spec can concretely embody the behavior a function performs.
Direction fits the spec's pattern that downstream technical layers realize application-layer elements, not the reverse.
arguments_against: The function definition explicitly excludes being offered as a contract to external consumers. An API operation is such a contract, so the design text does not support this edge.
There is no documentation in the facts explaining why operations target functions rather than services.

arguments_for: ArchiMate permits several readings of how concrete specifications relate to behavior. Whether operations trace to services, functions, or both is a product choice.
Adding an operation-to-service edge alongside, rather than reversing, is a design decision about traceability granularity.
Some codebases have internal APIs where an operation maps directly to a function with no distinct service.
arguments_against: The layer definitions already decide the question: externally visible offerings are services, internal behavior is functions.
A choice that contradicts the subject's own definition is less a trade-off than an inconsistency.

arguments_for: The relationship is sourced from the api layer, so arguably its ownership and review belong to that layer, not application.
arguments_against: The claim concerns a relationship schema in the spec itself, not tooling or an unmodelled concept.
The edge targets application.applicationfunction and directly affects how that type is used, so it is squarely in scope.
